title: [Audit] 🗂️ Kibana Object Forensics
description: Every Kibana saved-object read and change, by type, name, space and actor.

config.description: All Kibana audit events. Usually a small fraction of raw stream volume, but most of the forensic value — this is where saved objects, spaces and sessions are recorded.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" | STATS `Kibana events` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Every Kibana state change in range, selected by ECS event.type rather than by an action-name suffix. That matters: a suffix test cannot see rule_enable, rule_disable, the whole case_user_action family, or anything the workflow, ML and agent-builder features emit, because none of those action names end in _create/_update/_delete. Point-in-time open/close are ECS-tagged creation/deletion but are query internals, and are excluded by name.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | STATS `Mutations` = COUNT(*)

config.description: Distinct Kibana objects accessed or modified in range — reads included, as the name says. Identity is attributes.kibana.saved_object.id where Kibana records one and is recovered from body.text otherwise, because workflows, ML jobs and agent-builder tools carry no saved_object fields at all.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" | GROK body.text """\[(?:id|workflowId)=%{DATA:g_id}(?:,|\])""" | EVAL obj_id = COALESCE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.id, g_id) | STATS `Objects touched` = COUNT_DISTINCT(obj_id)

config.description: How many different kinds of thing were involved (dashboard, alert, index-pattern, tag, workflow …). Restricted to events that actually name an object: without that guard the derived type falls back to the action name and http_request — logged for every Kibana request — would count as an object type.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" | GROK body.text """\[(?:id|workflowId)=%{DATA:g_id}(?:,|\])""" | EVAL obj_id = COALESCE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.id, g_id) | EVAL obj_type = CASE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IS NOT NULL, attributes.kibana.saved_object.type, attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_job", "ml-job", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_datafeed", "ml-datafeed", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_execution_*", "workflow-execution", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_*", "workflow", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_agent_*", "agent-builder-agent", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_tool_*", "agent-builder-tool", attributes.event.action LIKE "product_documentation_*", "product-documentation", attributes.event.action == "secret_create", "secret", attributes.event.action IS NULL, "unclassified", REPLACE(attributes.event.action, "_(create|update|delete|enable|disable|run|run_soon|test|cancel)$", "")) | WHERE obj_id IS NOT NULL | STATS `Object types` = COUNT_DISTINCT(obj_type)

config.description: Distinct identities that changed anything in Kibana in range, resolved the same way every other actor panel resolves them. Counting emails alone misses changes made by credentials that carry no email. Includes people who only enabled a rule, ran a workflow or created an ML job — none of which an action-name suffix test counts as a change.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS `Editors` = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor)

config.title: ⚠️ Mutations — the 30 most recent Kibana state changes
config.description: The single most important panel in the suite: state changes in Kibana, with who did it, what it was called, and which space it lives in. These are the 30 most recent (scroll for the rest); every change in range is in "All mutations" on Security & Anomalies, and the "Kibana saved-object activity" session further down this page lists reads and changes together. Two columns to read carefully. Object type and Object are the real saved-object fields where Kibana records them and are otherwise recovered from the event message, because workflows, ML jobs and agent-builder objects carry no saved_object fields. A workflow cancel, or a test of an unsaved draft, names only its run, so it reads "execution" and the run id's first 8 characters. Result is "attempted" where Kibana logged the attempt rather than the outcome — that is how the saved-object path records things, so it is normal, and a "failure" here is a change that was denied.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE (resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" AND ((attributes.event.type IN ("change","creation","deletion") AND (attributes.event.action IS NULL OR NOT (attributes.event.action IN ("saved_object_open_point_in_time","saved_object_close_point_in_time")))) OR attributes.event.action IN ("rule_run_soon","secret_create"))) | EVAL verb = CASE(attributes.event.action LIKE "*_execution_cancel", "cancel", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run_soon", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_test", "test", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_enable", "enable", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_disable", "disable", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_put_*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_open_*", "open", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_start_*", "start", attributes.event.action LIKE "*point_in_time", "pit", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_create*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_update*", "update", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_delete", "delete", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_find", "find", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_get", "get", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_resolve", "resolve", "other") | GROK body.text """\[(?:id|workflowId)=%{DATA:g_id}(?:,|\])""" | GROK body.text """\[name=%{GREEDYDATA:g_name}\]""" | GROK body.text """\[executionId=%{DATA:g_exec}\]""" | GROK body.text """case id: %{NOTSPACE:g_case}""" | GROK body.text """(?:job|datafeed) %{NOTSPACE:g_ml}""" | EVAL obj_type = CASE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IS NOT NULL, attributes.kibana.saved_object.type, attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_job", "ml-job", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_datafeed", "ml-datafeed", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_execution_*", "workflow-execution", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_*", "workflow", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_agent_*", "agent-builder-agent", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_tool_*", "agent-builder-tool", attributes.event.action LIKE "product_documentation_*", "product-documentation", attributes.event.action == "secret_create", "secret", attributes.event.action IS NULL, "unclassified", REPLACE(attributes.event.action, "_(create|update|delete|enable|disable|run|run_soon|test|cancel)$", "")) | EVAL obj_name = COALESCE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.name, g_name, g_id, attributes.kibana.saved_object.id, g_case, g_ml, g_exec, body.text) | EVAL result = CASE(attributes.event.outcome == "unknown", "attempted", attributes.event.outcome) | EVAL execution = COALESCE(LEFT(g_exec, 8), "—") | EVAL is_exec = obj_name == g_exec | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_change = MAX(@timestamp) BY actor, verb, type = obj_type, name = obj_name, space = attributes.kibana.space.id, result, is_exec | SORT last_change DESC | LIMIT 30 | EVAL name = CASE(is_exec, CONCAT("execution ", LEFT(name, 8)), name)

config.title: Object type × operation
config.description: Saved-object type against operation, writes first. The more solid the cell, the more events it holds, on a log scale, so a single create, update or delete stays visible beside thousands of reads: the write columns are the forensic signal. Hover a cell for its count and how many distinct objects it covers.

config.title: Saved-object activity over time
config.description: Saved-object operations over time. Get, find, resolve and the other read verbs are folded into one "read" series, so each write verb keeps its own colour and the legend stays short enough to read.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IS NOT NULL | EVAL verb = CASE(attributes.event.action LIKE "*_execution_cancel", "cancel", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run_soon", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_test", "test", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_enable", "enable", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_disable", "disable", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_put_*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_open_*", "open", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_start_*", "start", attributes.event.action LIKE "*point_in_time", "pit", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_create*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_update*", "update", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_delete", "delete", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_find", "find", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_get", "get", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_resolve", "resolve", "other") | EVAL verb = CASE(verb IN ("get","find","resolve","pit","other"), "read", verb) | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY BUCKET(@timestamp, 75, ?_tstart, ?_tend), verb | SORT verb != "read", verb

config.title: Most-accessed objects by name
config.description: Real object titles from kibana.saved_object.name: the dashboards, rules and other objects people actually opened. Identities counts people and API keys alike, resolved the way every actor panel resolves them. Opening one of these audit dashboards is itself a read, so the suite's own dashboards and data view rank here in proportion to how much it is used.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.kibana.saved_object.name IS NOT NULL | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS events = COUNT(*), actors = COUNT_DISTINCT(actor) BY name = attributes.kibana.saved_object.name, type = attributes.kibana.saved_object.type | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Dashboards, SLOs and alert rules touched
config.description: Audit trail for the high-value object types only: who touched which dashboard, SLO, rule, workflow or ML job, and when. Both `alert` and `alerting_rule` are included, because Kibana records the same rule under either type depending on which code path audited it.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE resource.attributes.service.name == "serverless-kibana" | WHERE attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IS NOT NULL OR attributes.event.action IS NULL OR attributes.event.action != "http_request" | EVAL verb = CASE(attributes.event.action LIKE "*_execution_cancel", "cancel", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run_soon", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_run", "run", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_test", "test", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_enable", "enable", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_disable", "disable", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_put_*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_open_*", "open", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_start_*", "start", attributes.event.action LIKE "*point_in_time", "pit", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_create*", "create", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_update*", "update", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_delete", "delete", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_find", "find", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_get", "get", attributes.event.action LIKE "*_resolve", "resolve", "other") | GROK body.text """\[(?:id|workflowId)=%{DATA:g_id}(?:,|\])""" | GROK body.text """\[name=%{GREEDYDATA:g_name}\]""" | GROK body.text """\[executionId=%{DATA:g_exec}\]""" | GROK body.text """case id: %{NOTSPACE:g_case}""" | GROK body.text """(?:job|datafeed) %{NOTSPACE:g_ml}""" | EVAL obj_type = CASE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IS NOT NULL, attributes.kibana.saved_object.type, attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_job", "ml-job", attributes.event.action LIKE "ml_*ad_datafeed", "ml-datafeed", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_execution_*", "workflow-execution", attributes.event.action LIKE "workflow_*", "workflow", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_agent_*", "agent-builder-agent", attributes.event.action LIKE "agent_builder_tool_*", "agent-builder-tool", attributes.event.action LIKE "product_documentation_*", "product-documentation", attributes.event.action == "secret_create", "secret", attributes.event.action IS NULL, "unclassified", REPLACE(attributes.event.action, "_(create|update|delete|enable|disable|run|run_soon|test|cancel)$", "")) | EVAL obj_name = COALESCE(attributes.kibana.saved_object.name, g_name, g_id, attributes.kibana.saved_object.id, g_case, g_ml, g_exec, body.text) | WHERE obj_type IN ("dashboard","slo","alert","alerting_rule","tag","index-pattern","workflow","agent-builder-agent","agent-builder-tool","ml-job") | EVAL is_exec = obj_name == g_exec | EVAL actor = COALESCE(attributes.user.email, attributes.api_key.name, attributes.user.name, "<anonymous>"), actor_kind = CASE(attributes.user.email IS NOT NULL, "human", "service") | STATS events = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY actor, verb, type = obj_type, name = obj_name, is_exec | SORT last_seen DESC | LIMIT 10 | EVAL name = CASE(is_exec, CONCAT("execution ", LEFT(name, 8)), name)

config.title: Object types accessed
config.description: The ten saved-object types with the most traffic. Background reads by Kibana features and integrations can outweigh human activity; the heatmap above splits each type by operation.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.kibana.saved_object.type IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY type = attributes.kibana.saved_object.type | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Activity by space
config.description: Kibana activity in the ten busiest spaces. Viewing these audit dashboards counts too, so the space they are installed in carries their own reads.

data_source.query: FROM logs-elastic_cloud.serverless_audit.otel-default | WHERE @timestamp <= ?_tend AND @timestamp > ?_tstart | WHERE attributes.kibana.space.id IS NOT NULL | STATS events = COUNT(*) BY space = attributes.kibana.space.id | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 10

config.title: Cross-space activity
config.description: Identities ranked by how many Kibana spaces they touched. Anything above one space is worth understanding.

config.title: Kibana saved-object activity
config.description: Every Kibana event that named an object, reads and changes, newest first; the newest 1,000 in range. Kibana's page requests, logins and point-in-time internals name no object and are left out. Message is the sentence Kibana wrote for the event. Open in Discover to filter on a column or page further back.

config.title: Session reconstruction
config.description: One person's Kibana sessions, event by event, newest first: every object they opened and changed, with the sentence Kibana wrote for each. Pin an identity first, then open in Discover, filter to one Session and sort Time ascending to replay it forward. Kibana's internal UI requests and point-in-time internals are left out; public API calls such as an export are kept. Empty when nobody used Kibana in a browser in range: API-key traffic carries no session.
